text: Time to put this whole chapter together. This lab works through two real requests on the Incident table, start to finish, applying everything covered so far about timing, operation checks, previous, and avoiding the mistakes from last lesson.

Request one: when a new incident is created, automatically set its assignment group based on category, so agents aren't manually routing every ticket. Request two: when an incident's priority escalates to Critical, notify the assigned agent's manager, but only at the real moment it escalates, not on every later save.

Rule one is a before-insert rule. It checks current dot operation to confirm it's actually an insert, looks up the matching group by name, and sets assignment group directly on current. Because this is a before rule, that change is folded automatically into the one save already happening — no extra update call needed.

Rule two is an after-update rule, with Advanced enabled so it can access previous. It checks whether priority is now one and previous priority was not one — that comparison is what isolates the real escalation moment. Once confirmed, it looks up the assigned agent, finds their manager, and queues a notification event.

Notice what's deliberately avoided here. Neither rule writes back into the same table that triggered it, so there's no infinite loop. Rule one's operation check and its own insert-only checkbox agree with each other. Rule two carries a Filter Condition on priority changes, so its script body doesn't even run for edits that have nothing to do with priority.

That's the whole chapter in two working rules — correct timing, correct use of current and previous, and none of last lesson's five mistakes. Next, we move from server-side Business Rules to Client Scripts, starting with onLoad, onChange, onSubmit, and onCellEdit.
